_comment: A recorded run, so the page is fully developable and demoable without the agent or the
Grafana stack. Watchtower and Diagnostician payloads are the REAL output of the
2026-08-26 run against the seeded stack (9 and 6 tool calls, 45.0s and 66.1s).
The impact_forecaster stage is not built yet: its payload is invented, but every number
in it is one of the real measured numbers (1619 frames, 10.1 -> 5.5 fr/min, 2h18m slip).
Field names match second_unit/schemas.py exactly so the live stream can replace this
file with no client change. 'after_ms' is replay pacing only and is stripped by app.py.

output.summary: The render farm is experiencing significant frame failures on render-07 due to GPU faults, causing a substantial increase in the lighting department's render queue depth.
error_signatures: CUDA error: uncorrectable ECC error encountered (cudaErrorECCUncorrectable) at kernel launch
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:41:00): 48, pid=0, GPU has fallen off the bus. uncorrectable ECC error encountered on GPU 0
level=error service=render-scheduler shot=SH042 department=lighting frame=1184 node=render-07 exit_code=139 msg="frame failed, requeueing" retry=1/3

evidence.claim: The lighting queue is more than three times its normal depth.
evidence.observed: lighting=62, animation=9, fx=14, comp=6 — lighting sat at 18 before 02:14.

evidence.claim: Frame failures are confined to a single node.
evidence.observed: render-07=47. No other node returned a series.

evidence.claim: render-07 is logging uncorrectable ECC faults at the driver level.
evidence.observed: 41 lines since 02:14, all node=render-07, all Xid 48 / cudaErrorECCUncorrectable.

output.root_cause: The GPU in render-07 is failing due to a hardware fault, likely related to overheating, which is causing all of its assigned render frames to fail.
causal_chain: The GPU on render-07 is running at 80-86 C against a peer range of 60-65 C.
That thermal stress manifests as GPU instability, logged as uncorrectable ECC errors and NVRM Xid 48.
Every frame of SH042's lighting pass scheduled onto render-07 fails with exit code 139.
The render-scheduler requeues each failed frame onto the same faulty node, forming a failure loop.
The lighting department's queue depth climbs as requeued frames accumulate faster than they clear.

hypotheses.statement: Render node render-07 has a critical hardware fault with its GPU
hypotheses.reasoning: render-07 reports 80-86 C GPU temperature while its peers sit at 60-65 C, and it is the only node emitting uncorrectable ECC and Xid 48 events. Every failed frame in the last 90 minutes was assigned to it.

hypotheses.statement: Other render nodes (render-01, 08, 09, 10, 11) are also failing and contributing
hypotheses.reasoning: increase(render_frames_failed_total[90m]) returns a series for render-07 only. The other five nodes report zero failures and normal GPU temperatures.

hypotheses.statement: The issue is caused by a bug in the render software for SH042 or the lighting department
hypotheses.reasoning: SH042 lighting frames scheduled onto healthy nodes complete normally, and lighting log lines excluding render-07 contain no render-software errors. The failure follows the node, not the shot or the department.

evidence.claim: render-07's GPU is 20 C hotter than every peer node.
All frame failures in the last 90 minutes belong to one node and one reason.
The driver has been resetting the GPU since 02:14.
evidence.observed: First Xid 48 at 02:14:07, most recent 41s ago; 41 occurrences, none on any other node.

evidence.claim: The scheduler is returning failed frames to the node that failed them.
evidence.observed: retry=1/3 then retry=2/3 for frame 1184, both dispatched to node=render-07.

notes: 1,619 frames at 5.5 fr/min is 4h 54m of wall clock; at the 10.1 fr/min baseline it is 2h 40m.
Recovering the healthy pool alone does not save the review: render-07 must be drained so the scheduler stops requeueing onto it.
Three lighting artists are blocked on this pass from 08:00 and have no fallback task queued.

evidence.claim: SH042's lighting pass has 1,619 frames left to render.

evidence.observed: 5.5 frames/min now against a 10.1 frames/min pre-incident baseline.

td.headline: render-07 GPU is throwing uncorrectable ECC — lighting capacity −46%
td.sub: Xid 48 since 02:14, 138 frames failed exit 139 in 90m, all on one node. Peers clean. Scheduler is requeueing onto the fault.
td.action: Drain render-07 from the lighting pool, requeue SH042 frames 1184–2803 to render-01/08/09, raise a hardware ticket on the GPU.
td.risk: Draining costs 1 of 6 nodes; the remaining pool clears the backlog at 9.4 fr/min.

supervisor.headline: SH042's lighting pass is 2h 18m behind, and one node is the cause
supervisor.sub: render-07 is failing every frame it is given. Nothing is wrong with the shot, the lighting setup, or the other five nodes.
supervisor.action: Approve draining render-07. SH042 then lands about 16 minutes before the review instead of 2h 18m after it.
supervisor.risk: No creative rework needed — no frame rendered on a healthy node has failed.

producer.headline: SH042 misses Friday's 14:00 client review by 2h 18m
producer.sub: One faulty render machine. Three lighting artists idle from 08:00. Fixable now without overtime or a rescheduled review.
producer.action: Approve the fix and the review holds. Do nothing and the delivery lands at 16:18.
producer.risk: Cost of the fix: one machine offline for repair. Cost of waiting: the review slot.
